title: Path variables and request parameters
summary: Read values from a URL path, query string or form.

richText: Read a value from the path
@PathVariable reads a value captured by a {name} segment in a mapped path.
Use it for a resource identifier.
Spring converts the value to the Java parameter type. A value that cannot be converted normally produces a 400 response.

example.title: Read a user ID from the URL
description: Place this method in a @RestController. Send GET /users/123.
explanation: {id} captures 123. @PathVariable("id") passes it to id as an int.
The method returns text identifying the requested ID. It does not look up a user.

richText: @RequestParam reads a named query parameter or a form parameter.
Query parameters follow ? in a URL. Use them for search, filtering or sorting.
A @RequestParam is required by default. Use required = false or Optional for an optional value.
defaultValue supplies a value when the parameter is missing or empty. It also makes the parameter optional.
An array or List can receive repeated values for the same parameter name.
Use @RequestParam for form data. Use @RequestBody for a JSON body.

example.title: Use a default search value
description: Place this method in a @RestController. Send GET /users/search?name=Alice.
explanation: The query parameter name becomes the Java argument name.
For this request the method returns Search: Alice.
GET /users/search without a name value returns Search: all.
This method demonstrates reading input; it does not perform a database search.

richText: A handler can use both @PathVariable and @RequestParam. Each annotation identifies where its argument comes from.
